title: An illustrative travel vessel

passage.edition: World English Bible Classic (linked, not bundled)

summary: A small technical example for packaging a passage-linked 3D object. Genesis 12:5 mentions possessions carried on the journey. This vessel is an invented visual aid, not an object specified by that verse.
limitations: The passage does not identify this vessel, its shape, material, maker or date. No archaeological identification is claimed. This package is not a complete chapter experience or production-quality art.

files.creator: BibleHorizons contributors
files.changes: Original procedural example; no third-party model or textures.

provenance.rightsEvidence: Original geometry authored for this kit and offered under CC BY 4.0.

hotspots.label: The passage connection
hotspots.description: Genesis 12:5 mentions possessions brought on the journey. This example uses an invented vessel to show how a proposed object can link to the passage without claiming the text describes that object.

hotspots.label: What is imagined
hotspots.description: The rounded form and earthen color are artistic choices for this technical example. They are not sourced evidence for the appearance of Abram’s possessions.

coverage.description: Only the mention of possessions is used as context. The object is invented; other people, movements and events in this verse are outside this asset-only example.
